task: Implement Chinese-first human-facing content policy and evaluate Prism timeout follow-up risks
user_intent: Norven authorized execution. The repository should enforce that human-facing content is Chinese-first, readable for humans, avoids machine/AI jargon and isolated workflow-node nouns, while allowing necessary professional terms with immediate Chinese explanations. Norven also asked whether the previously identified Prism timeout future risks should be fixed in the same batch.
main_claim: This batch should add executable safeguards for the human-facing language policy, then implement only the Prism timeout follow-ups that are currently bounded, testable, and not likely to expand into a broad scheduler redesign.
changed_reality: The current dispatcher already has per-provider attempt timeout, total provider-call timeout, process-group cleanup, timeout raw evidence, and expired provider session marking.
The language policy exists only as a user instruction in conversation and is not yet embedded in repository instructions, checks, or templates.
Known timeout follow-up risks include whole-task multi-provider budget, automatic timeout decision policy, remote provider session continuation uncertainty, and Chinese readable timeout reports.
proposal: Add a Chinese-first human-facing content contract in repository assets and wire it into RedCap checks so the rule is executable, not only remembered.

Add a checker that scans likely human-facing repository files and rejects obvious banned wording patterns and unexplained first-use professional terms where feasible without pretending to solve natural-language quality perfectly.
Improve Prism timeout outputs so timeout records and user summaries are human-readable in Chinese while preserving structured machine fields.
Add a bounded timeout policy helper that classifies provider timeout outcomes into continue-with-other-reviewer, retry, or Cap arbitration, without building a full automatic provider scheduler.
Defer whole-task multi-provider wall-clock budgeting and remote provider hard-stop guarantees unless a narrow implementation is available without redesigning Prism orchestration.
non_goals: Do not claim perfect natural-language quality detection.
Do not edit third-party raw provider output.
Do not add providers beyond Kimi and Claude Code.
Do not build a full autonomous multi-provider scheduler in this batch.
Do not start the 360 old RedCap scan in this batch.
review_questions: Which parts of the Chinese-first policy must be executable now instead of documentation only?
Which Prism timeout follow-up risks are bounded enough to fix now?
What checks should block regressions without making normal answers impossible?
What should remain explicit future work because it needs a larger scheduler or host integration design?
expected_output: Return strict JSON with provider, verdict, confidence, reality_delta, main_concern, top_risks, missing_evidence, minimum_fix, anti_loop_signal, and user_intent_alignment.
